column1: # Planted flaws and the tests that must catch them. scripts/check-flaws.sh
# runs each row with JOBQUEUE_FLAW=<id> and the jobqueue_flaws build tag, and
# requires a test to go red. Columns, separated by tabs:
#   id       the flaw (internal/flaw/flaw.go); every flaw needs at least one row
#   regex    the test that must fail, as go test -run takes it
#   tags     - or pg (adds the pg tag and needs JOBQUEUE_TEST_DSN)
#   expect   - or text that the failing output must contain
# expect is set where a failure could have another cause. A flaw clause that
# has drifted from its statement panics the whole package in init, and a pg
# test without a database fails too; neither is the flaw being noticed. The
# differential rows name "reference store", which every divergence message of
# TestPGDifferential contains and neither of those can. The simulator rows
# name the invariant that the flaw must break (a violation reads "S4 violated
# for job ..."), which also shows the flaw is caught by the check that is meant
# to catch it. A flaw with a row in two packages needs both caught.
# Memory store: caught by the conformance suite.
# Simulator: the sweep of 500 seeds finds each memory-store flaw and F5 through
# the invariant named in expect. The seed count must stay at its default: F1-mem
# is the rarest, found by 17 of 500 seeds.
# Postgres store: caught by the differential test, which holds pgstore to the
# memory store, and by the concurrency tests for the two flaws that only show
